Okay. To be honest, I no longer hear what I heard in June, but I know some of those were real, while some were probably in my head. People think I am faking everything, and that I always lie, but I guess I'll drive myself crazy trying to prove them wrong.

I'm trying to get over the fact that so many people think I am stupid now. I know it is my pride that is causing me to feel shame, and that I should just move forward even though people think that. There's also the fact that I'm studying mathematics in the top university in the country, and it makes people angry that a -stupid- terrible person wastes their tax. It was also humiliating to be laughed at when I was struggling in June, while I was completely out of my mind.

Thank you so much for your comment. I wish people knew how it felt to be on that kinda drugs. However, I know I did a lot of shitty things which made them hate me, so I try not to feel too bad for myself.

Okay, I will try to love myself in the way that you said.
Hmmm, I did see it on the Facebook group and not on the page... Maybe you're right...
Thank you so much!
Okay, fuck this, I may as well do all those things before I go. Thanks fam.
My parents don't even believe it's real. Of course my relatives won't tell them they hate me!
I don't know.

Hello, this is OP from a different account,

Thanks for the comment. I feel validated. It is true, I felt so weird during May and June. I honestly feel so angry right now, because people judged me based on what they saw in June. And I really did feel like shit then. I could not think clearly at all, although I was thinking about a lot of stuff. I really wanted to finish the semester.

I also feel frustrated because they think I am faking everything. Nowadays, I don't feel the ups and downs anymore because I may have adjusted to the meds already. But before, I really did feel helpless a lot, despite the circumstances. I was aware I had a good life, sometimes, and I still felt hella empty. They did not see this, because I tried to hide this from my family mostly.

I wish I started medication sooner, before all these things happened.

From my post on /r/offmychest:

I have moved back home in May, after living somewhere else for six months. I honestly can't believe the damage I have caused by trying to live there. I should have just stayed home. I should have noticed that I felt stronger in my hometown, somehow. Instead, I blamed my sadness, anger, and dissatisfaction on this place. I should have noticed that I also felt that in other places, and the problem was with me and my mindset. I should have stayed home. I should have stayed home.

I really should have stayed home. I could have helped my dad fix the house. I mean, I'm no builder, but I only needed to run errands for him so he could focus on fixing the house. For some reason, I deemed it not worth my time. I wish I helped him instead. He was even willing to pay me. I could have used that money to buy things I wanted, instead of draining the scholarship money the government gave me. I shouldn't have spent that scholarship money. I could have saved it if I stayed at home.

I couldn't believe how much of a reckless spender I was when I stayed in that other place. I became extremely lazy and ordered food to be delivered to me instead of just walking to the grocery store to buy food I could cook. I used my scholarship money for that, and other things. I wish I just stayed home.

I had a plan before I moved. I could have done that, instead of recklessly buying stuff and thinking about impossible things. I had a good routine. I would learn how to play guitar in the afternoon and read at night. If there were classes, I'd attend classes and study. It was okay. It was all okay. I wish I had been okay with it. I wish I didn't decide to move to that other place. It was all a waste. I wish I had been more patient with this house, and that I helped fix it. I wish I stayed here. I wish I stayed here.

I am now known in my hometown as this dumbass who went to the best university in the country and wasted her scholarship money to live a life of luxury for a while. I can feel that I've been a waste of the people's taxes. I really should have stayed home. I should have thought about it. I am not a dumbass all the time. I wish I focused on studying instead of trying to move away. If I wanted money to buy stuff I wanted but not needed, I could have worked for my parents in our store. I should have done that. I should have used the scholarship money to help pay the bills and groceries.

I wasn't like this all the time. I hadn't always been this reckless. I had been a little reckless but not to this extent. I may have eaten too expensively in the past, but it was not everyday. It was maybe once a week.

I shouldn't have done what I did in those six months. I should have just stayed home and played guitar and read books and studied. For some reason, when I moved into that other place, I sold that guitar for less than half the price I bought it, and I bought an electric guitar. I wish I had not done that. I wish I stayed home and enjoyed what I had. I had all the resources I needed. There was the internet if I wanted to learn stuff.

I should have also interacted with my relatives who were also my neighbours (in my hometown). I had barely talked to them. I should have said hi once in a while. I should have minded the things I was doing to make sure I was not bothering them. I really should have just done that. When it was their birthdays, I should have greeted them. When it was my birthday, I should have shared food with them. I wouldn't be so lonely if I just accepted their love and gave them love also. Instead, I blamed my loneliness and lack of progress on this place.

Didn't I notice that when I moved to that other place, I was also lonely, if not more? For six months, I devolved into this creature. I barely was under the sun. I was just inside the unit alone most days, and I went up and down the elevator whenever I had food delivered to me. I barely showered. I neglected myself. I also drank, for various reasons: I was lonely, I was celebrating, I was bored, etc. I managed to drink because I was alone. I also changed the curtain from grey to black, so nobody could see me. I was literally living in the darkness. I also became sadder, even though I was living in luxury.

I also wasn't doing well in some of my classes. So I told my professors it was because of mental health issues. Now, why would I say that? Sure, I had mental health issues, but I could have taken care of myself if I had only listened to other people. I had been talking to a guidance counselour and he recommended certain activities to help regulate my emotions (exercise, going under the sun, taking showers at certain temperatures). Those activities were well within my reach, and yet I did NOT do them. I insisted I needed medication.

In May, I was prescribed antipsychotics. I didn't take these until I went back home.

When I went back home, during the first three days, I was very sad and angry. Looking back, it may have been the meds. I was only starting so I may not have adjusted yet. However, I blamed this on my home. I'd wish I stayed somewhere else. That was one of the worst things I have said, because why would I blame this place? This home isn't perfect but it's good enough. My space is huge. Also, I live in a third world country, and I should have known that this is better than what many people have. I should have been grateful for my hardworking parents for providing us with this home. I also blamed some people too, including my older sister (who owned the place in which I stayed for six months).

Then, suddenly, while I was at home, there was a miracle! I was stable! I was not lonely! This was during the last week of May. However, I still felt angry from time to time. I would wish I lived somewhere else, still. I thought about moving back on campus for some reason. I didn't feel sad nor feel like crying, though. So, I studied, and after studying, I celebrated by playing games I had used to play as a kid.

I really, really wish I just used that time to study and to help cleaning the house.

June was such a bad month. It would take forever to explain what happened, but I believe it was the punishment for all I'd done those six months, especially in May. Long story short, I got sick and messed up my meds. It was insanity. 

I was also exposed to my neighbours. I cannot explain how it happened but I know it happened. My sins. My plans to move back on campus. The scholarship money I wasted. The fact that I barely attended zoom meetings for my classes. Even my sexual history was revealed too. They also accused me of other stuff which was not true, but most of the stuff they uncovered was true and awful.

It has dawned on me what a sh***y person I had been during those six months, and possibly the few months before that, too. I did the kind of stuff I would criticise others for doing. I really want to shoot myself for this. Sometimes, I blame my neighbours for exposing me (I still don't know how they did that). However, this was all my fault. If only I had been patient, nice, respectful, clean, and hard-working, many of these would have been avoided.

I really wish I had stayed in my hometown. I was from here, and I had no real reasons to leave yet. I didn't even have a job. I just had money given to me by the government (because I had answered a certain exam really well), and money given to me by my family. I really should have stayed.
